title: OTAS Settlement Instruction
description: A rail-neutral settlement instruction: the common construct by which two heterogeneous systems express and verify an instruction's state, while the atomicity mechanism beneath it (HTLC, escrow/notary, shared ledger) is deliberately NOT prescribed. Lifecycle: PROPOSED -> COMMITTED -> SETTLED | ABORTED. Once the coordinator holds both legs' states the instruction moves to COMMITTED: enqueued, will not be lost, and no longer revocable by a participant. That transition is the revocability boundary and a natural anchor for legal finality; SETTLED marks final settlement. Each leg declares its technical finality model and its legal-finality construct, because atomicity alone delivers neither.

timeout_policy.description: Per-leg timeouts; in an HTLC the asset-leg timeout must exceed the cash-leg timeout to avoid the free-option asymmetry

netting.description: Liquidity-saving mechanisms are describable, not impossible: a leg may reference a netting window or queue rather than a gross pre-funded amount.

finality.description: Both the finality model and the finality moment are declared, rather than inferred from atomicity.

confirmation_depth.description: For a probabilistic rail: the depth at which this leg is treated as settled

regime_ref.description: The governing rulebook or jurisdictional construct

abort_after_committed.description: Whether this rulebook permits Abort after Committed, e.g. on exceptional technical failure

lock_ref.description: Rail-native reference to the escrow/lock once the leg's state is held (e.g. an EVM lock id, a Sui escrow account)
